subject: Service guarantee boundaries & SLA measurement - finalizing redlines
messages:
From: Evan Blake <evan.blake@brightwavehealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Review <legal@brightwavehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2029 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final SLA points from BrightWave

Alex — thanks for your time today. Quick follow-up from BrightWave's side as we try to close the commercial review: we want to confirm a few SLA items so procurement can sign off.

Key asks from our side: 
- Uptime target: 99.95% measured monthly (calendar month).
- Scheduled maintenance: allow up to 6 hours / calendar month; needs at least 72 hours notice.
- Response times: P1 (platform down): 1 hour response & continuous remediation updates; P2 (partial impact): 4 hours.
- Service credits: cumulative credits up to 30% of monthly subscription for breaches; credits to be applied on next invoice.
- Evidence: require access to incident logs and a monthly availability report.

If you can confirm these or send counter-language we can push legal to finalize.

Thanks,
Evan Blake
Director, Cloud Ops
BrightWave Health

Attachment: none
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Blake <evan.blake@brightwavehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2029 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final SLA points from BrightWave

Evan — appreciate the clear list. I attached our redlined Order Form (OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) with inline language that reflects where we think we can land quickly. High-level counter-proposals below and comments for your legal team.

Summary of Redwood positions: 
- Availability metric: we prefer Measurement at the public API endpoint (Subscription Availability) across the provisioned region, computed as a rolling 30-day availability percentage to reduce edge-month anomalies. See the attached SLA_margin_calc.xlsx for examples.
- Scheduled maintenance: standard 72-hour notice for planned maintenance <=4 hours. Planned windows >4 hours will require 5 business days notice. Scheduled maintenance will be excluded from uptime calculations only if posted and acknowledged in the maintenance registry.
- Response times: we’ll commit to 1-hour acknowledge for P1 and a remediation update cadence every 2 hours until resolved. P2 acknowledge within 4 hours; resolution target depends on impact.
- Service credits: propose a cap at 25% of monthly fees (applies to cumulative breaches in a given month) and credits applied as a bill adjustment.
- Evidence: we can provide per-incident telemetry export (S3 link) and a standardized monthly availability report. We cannot provide raw customer-trace logs due to data isolation policies, but we will provide aggregated telemetry and timestamps to validate uptime calculations.

Kimberly — I flagged a few legal points inline in the redline PDF. Vivek / Ops — can you confirm whether the rolling 30-day calc is feasible and whether the maintenance registry approach will be operationally reliable?

Next step: if BrightWave agrees to the above in principle, Kimberly can produce clean contract language and we can move to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0199

Attachments: OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (pdf); SLA_margin_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Evan Blake <evan.blake@brightwavehealth.com>, Legal Review <legal@brightwavehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2029 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final SLA points from BrightWave

Thanks — I reviewed the redline. A few legal comments/usability constraints to surface for BrightWave before we finalize: 

1) Measurement window: calendar month is preferred by procurement for billing simplicity. If BrightWave requires rolling 30-day, please confirm they accept the operational implications — we'll need to reflect that in invoicing language.

2) Scheduled maintenance: require clearer "notice" and approval mechanics. Propose the following compromise text: 
- Routine maintenance <=4 hours: 72 hours notice.
- Maintenance >4 hours: 5 business days notice and explicit customer acknowledgment (email reply or portal ack).

3) Service credits cap: 25% is acceptable, but we need explicit definitions of breach buckets (e.g., <99.5%, 99.5-99.95%, etc.) so credit calculation is deterministic. I can draft the tier table.

4) Evidence & audits: we cannot provide raw customer data. Offer: monthly availability report + incident packet (aggregated telemetry + SLO calculation) submitted within 10 business days of the month's end. For disputes, both parties agree to leverage a joint time-limited forensic review (scope limited to metadata) rather than open-ended log access.

Kimberly Park
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

On the operational side, Vivek — can you confirm whether the registry approach for scheduled maintenance will produce the artifacts Legal needs (ID, timestamp, notice copy)?
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Evan Blake <evan.blake@brightwavehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jul 2029 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final SLA points from BrightWave

Quick ops perspective: rolling 30-day calculation is operationally straightforward on our side (we run daily aggregates) and reduces edge cases where upgrades at month boundaries spike credit exposure. We can produce a signed maintenance registry entry with: maintenance_id, scheduled_start/end, published_notice (HTML), and an acceptance flag when customer uses the portal ack. That registry artifact should be sufficient for exclusion.

A few caveats: 
- For short emergency mitigations (<1 hour) we treat as P1 but will not retroactively exclude impact unless there was a prior maintenance registry entry.
- Some remediation (KV-cache flush, DB failovers) can cause transient errors that do not affect Subscription Availability as defined; I suggest we codify "successful request rate at API gateway" as the measuring signal to avoid disputed noise.
- Evidence delivery: we will publish a per-month S3 bundle (aggregated telemetry + calculation workbook) and a signed hash for provenance. I'll add a docs link.

Operational ask to BrightWave: indicate whether portal ack is acceptable or they require an email-based acknowledgment flow. Portal ack is preferred for automation.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Blake <evan.blake@brightwavehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jul 2029 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final SLA points from BrightWave — proposed compromise and next steps

Evan — based on the thread above, here's a short set of compromise items we can present to procurement/legal at BrightWave. If you can confirm with a simple "accept in principle" we will hand to our legal ops team and generate a DocuSign packet.

Proposed compromise (high level):
- Measurement: Subscription Availability measured at the API gateway. Primary calculation: calendar month, with optionally visible rolling 30-day series for operational context. Credits will be calculated on the calendar month but legal will include a reference to a 30-day smoothing methodology in the appendix to reduce boundary anomalies.
- Maintenance exclusion: routine maintenance <=4 hours: 72 hours notice (portal ack preferred). Maintenance >4 hours: 5 business days notice + portal ack. Emergency maintenance exclusions limited and require post-incident declaration + registry entry to be excluded from credit calculations.
- Response times: P1 acknowledge within 1 hour, with remediation updates every 2 hours. P2 acknowledge within 4 hours.
- Credits: capped at 25% of monthly fees. Credit tiers will be defined in a deterministic table (Kim will draft). Credits applied as invoice adjustments on next billing cycle.
- Evidence: Redwood to publish a monthly S3 bundle with aggregated telemetry and a signed hash within 10 business days of month-end; defect packet provided within 5 business days of incident close. For disputed calculations, both parties will agree to a scoped forensic review before external audit escalation.

Attachments: SLA_summary_for_exec.docx (summary for procurement)

If BrightWave accepts, Kimberly will produce clean contract language and we will send the DocuSign link (see related links). Evan — can you respond with a short acceptance or indicate any remaining non-starters?

Best,
Alex Martinez
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
